currentContract.chronology: 58 ordered tier-1 scripts, then 41 ordered tier-2 scripts

evidence.phase7dA: actual current loaders are browser-hard-gated for exact insertion/execution/load chronology, parent placement, async=false and tier-2 duplicate guards
evidence.phase7dB: all 41 tier-2 entries are exact-byte mapped by authority class and predecessor constraints, including V581A cross-tier predecessors
evidence.phase7dC: a dormant flat-loader prototype reproduces the accepted symbolic 45 -> 41 order without reading, requiring or executing production v40-release.js

alternatives.description: Keep config.js and v40-release.js byte-identical and retain the current nested loader.
Change the frozen v40-release.js so it coordinates tier-2 loading only after the remaining tier-1 chain completes.
alternatives.protectedBoundaryChanges: v40-release exact frozen blob plus loader/seal/chronology checkpoints

alternatives.description: Replace the staged v40-release.js entry with a new production successor that owns release presentation plus deferred tier-2 transport.
alternatives.productionSiteChanges: site/config.js plus a new site successor file
alternatives.protectedBoundaryChanges: Option 2A/2B/2C successor authorization, Option 2C config exact successor, loader manifest and chronology checkpoints

alternatives.description: Remove v40-release.js from the staged runtime and move both its release-presentation boundary and flat tier-2 transport into config.js.
alternatives.productionSiteChanges: site/config.js plus retirement semantics for site/v40-release.js
alternatives.protectedBoundaryChanges: Option 2C config exact successor, loader manifest, release-presentation ownership, chronology/seal checkpoints

reasons: The current nested chronology is deterministic and machine-enforced; no active loader correctness defect remains.
The dormant flat prototype proves feasibility but does not reveal a functional behavior improvement over the current production contract.
A production successor file saves zero runtime script requests; the most aggressive config-inline variant saves only one of 86 runtime script requests.
Changing v40-release.js crosses exact frozen-blob boundaries, while adding/replacing a production successor crosses the maintained site-successor and loader-manifest contracts.
Release identity already derives from the staged list and is not dependent on v40-release.js being the highest-version owner, so there is no release-identity defect to fix.
Phase 7D explicitly requires stopping before runtime work when the expected benefit is only a trivial request-count reduction without broader proven payoff.

dormantFallback.purpose: reusable successor proof if a future architectural need justifies reopening the protected loader boundary

reopenOnlyIf: a reproducible production defect is attributable to the nested loader itself
a future multi-module bundling plan is blocked solely by the nested loader and offers material request/latency reduction beyond the current one-request ceiling
a browser/platform change invalidates the hard-gated current chronology
a broader release architecture change already requires coordinated config/v40-release and seal successor work
rollback: No runtime rollback is needed because Phase 7D-D authorizes no production change. If reopened later, the current exact config.js/v40-release.js blobs remain the rollback reference.
